sources.title: Prehistory of Western Siberia: The Lower Ob in the first millennium
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of Lower Ob first-millennium sites, Orontur chronology, pottery, settlements, and interpretive limits.

sources.title: Samoyedic: General introduction
sources.note: Authoritative linguistic overview of the Samoyedic branch, its several languages, reconstruction, and geographic diversity.

sources.title: Orontur type of archaeological sites
sources.note: Expert synthesis of sixth- to ninth-century western Siberian sites, houses, burials, tools, crafts, subsistence, and exchange.

sources.title: Taymyr: The Archaeology of Northernmost Eurasia
sources.note: Smithsonian monograph on Taymyr sites, ceramics, chronology, environmental adaptation, movement, and evidentiary gaps.

sources.title: The Agan River and Its Inhabitants
sources.note: Regional scholarly publication describing eighth- to ninth-century fortified plans, houses, pottery, and material culture.

sources.title: Yugra in the early medieval period
sources.note: Institutional archaeology teaching resource on Kuchimino chronology, settlement finds, burials, bronze work, and weapon display.

sources.title: Twenty Years of Northern Archaeological Research
sources.note: Northern Archaeology Institute report on rescue excavations, short-term settlements, organic preservation, and chronological revision.

sources.title: Archaeology of the Russian North: From the Iron Age to the Russian Empire
sources.note: Conference volume on river-terrace site distributions, Yamal seasonal settlements, site visibility, and regional sampling.

sources.title: A Medieval Child Burial at Lake Parisento, Gydan Peninsula
sources.note: Russian Academy report on a securely studied but later 900 to 1100 infant burial and imported objects.

sources.title: The Samoyed languages
sources.note: Modern linguistic synthesis of language diversity, uneven documentation, early word lists, and twentieth-century writing systems.

sources.title: Best practices in justifying calibrations for dating language families
sources.note: Peer-reviewed methodological study using Uralic evidence to explain uncertainty in language divergence dates.

sources.title: Towards an integrated account of Northern Samoyedic history
sources.note: Peer-reviewed language-contact synthesis emphasizing dialect continua and interaction in Northern Samoyedic history.

sources.title: Interactive Atlas of Indigenous Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East
sources.note: Institutional Indigenous-peoples atlas explaining later ethnonyms and the distinct histories of Nenets, Enets, Nganasan, and Selkup.

sources.title: Northern Selkup language
sources.note: Russian Academy authored profile of Northern Selkup naming, dialects, multilingualism, documentation, education, and writing history.

sources.title: Forest Enets language
sources.note: Institutional profile explaining family and clan naming, language distinctions, and historically shifting classifications.

sources.title: Nganasan language
sources.note: Institutional profile of Nganasan documentation and the much later history of its written form.

sources.title: Tundra Nenets language
sources.note: Institutional profile dating missionary dictionaries, translations, grammars, and later educational use.

sources.title: Craniology and odontology of early medieval western Siberian populations
sources.note: Peer-reviewed biological anthropology study combining small regional samples and demonstrating the limits of group inference.

sources.title: Archaeology and Scientific Methods, issue 220
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology volume on western Siberian iron production, tools, and chronological evidence.

sources.title: Yamal: Code of Civilization
sources.note: Museum exhibition on deep regional history, Indigenous material culture, archaeological discovery, and local continuity.

sources.title: Interdisciplinary Study of the Multilayer Yamgort I Settlement
sources.note: Russian Archaeology study of an early medieval river settlement using soil chemistry, dwelling depressions, pottery, and cultural layers.

sources.title: Vozhpay and Kintus archaeological cultures
sources.note: Institutional archaeology resource on ninth-century continuation, later settlements, pottery, burials, and cautious ancestry interpretations.

sources.title: Enets
sources.note: Expert ethnological reference separating later Forest and Tundra Enets histories and warning against uniform projection.

sources.title: Nenets
sources.note: Estonian language institute reference on self-designation, late scholarly documentation, and nineteenth-century grammars.
